clue.text: The rabbit initially, like the hawk, died after having been skinned without 20

indicators.note: the rest of the pieces are placed after the words for being skinned

parts.note: a skinned rabbit has no fur left on it, read as two words
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word rabbit

parts.note: a hawk in politics is someone in favour of war, read as two words
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of a rabbit, killed and skinned by a hawk, getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places THE + R + FOR WAR + D after NO FUR. The 20 in the definition is the answer to 20 across, PROGRESS: without progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Making no headway means being without advancement, the plain sense of the phrase.

clue.text: The good European backing the good arms manufacturer?

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the French phrase from its end to its start

parts.note: le bon is French, a European language, for 'the good'

explanation.surface: A virtuous European supporting a benevolent weapons maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LE BON round. Alfred Nobel made dynamite and armaments, then left his fortune for the peace prizes, hence 'the good' arms manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the explosives and arms magnate, is remembered as a benefactor through his prizes.

clue.text: Flower unsuitable as present, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: the future tense is not the present tense, so it cannot serve as present

explanation.surface: A flower that would not make a suitable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it is the grammatical tense. In British speech the flower's name sounds close to FUTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a garden shrub grown for its drooping, colourful blooms.

clue.text: Not like Naomi to be so cruel

definitions.meaning: in the Bible Naomi had her daughter-in-law ... beside her; to lack ... is to be unlike her

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as RUTH + LESS, having no Ruth, in contrast to Naomi, whom Ruth famously refused to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no pity or compassion is the everyday meaning, a direct synonym of cruel.

clue.text: Key to the mess?

definitions.meaning: the # key on a keyboard or phone
a muddle or jumble, as in making a botch of something

explanation.definitionFit: The # symbol has this name on keypads, and to make a muddle of something is to make one of these.

clue.text: Start a fight with man in shearing shed

parts.note: to rouse is to stir or wake, to start up
a bout is a contest or fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A labourer picking a quarrel among the sheep shearers.
explanation.walkthrough: A rouseabout is the Australian and New Zealand name for an unskilled hand in a shearing shed who sweeps and gathers fleeces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian usage this is the general labourer in a shearing team, so a man found in the shed.

clue.text: Gas keeps fruit and veg deep-fried

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A gas cooker preserving fruit and frying vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is CS, the riot-control gas, and 'keeps' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Potato cut into strips and deep-fried is the British dish of this name.

clue.text: Conical hat for some cricketers backed — I think — by electric wire

indicators.note: backed asks for the selected letters to be read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the word cricketers is used

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise made when one is thinking
a flex is a flexible insulated electric cable

explanation.surface: Headgear for a cricket team, supported by a hesitant remark and a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes CRIC from cricketers and 'backed' turns it into CIRC. The circumflex accent ^ looks like a little pointed hat over a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The accent mark ^ is shaped like a pointed cap sitting on a letter, a visual description.

clue.text: Trouble positively start turning up — like woodlice

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: start means only the opening run of the word positively is used

explanation.surface: Trouble rising up, as with an infestation of woodlice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes POSI from positively; 'turning up' reverses ADO + POSI to give the zoological order.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlice belong to this order of crustaceans, so the order's name describes creatures of their kind.

clue.text: Unable to swallow? Apply 51cc paste mix

indicators.note: mix tells us to rearrange the combined letters

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying a measured dose of paste that cannot be swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to swallow' means unable to believe a story, not unable to gulp; 'mix' is the anagram signal and 'Apply' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to believe it, so being doubtful means being unable to accept it.

clue.text: 13? 1 19? Defender to make it all right with a person

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or hockey
taken as written
to square someone is to settle matters with them
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A defender trying to make amends with someone after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The definitions are cross-references: 13 down is FALSE START and 1/19 is NO FURTHER FORWARD, both returning you to where you began.
explanation.definitionFit: A false start or failing to advance leaves you starting over again from the beginning.

clue.text: See 3
Lover with stronghold to scale

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or lover
a fort is a fortified place

explanation.surface: A lover joins a fortress to climb the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like a verb, to climb; it is the Beaufort scale of wind force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort scale is the numbered measure of wind strength, so the name stands for that scale.

clue.text: Facts and figures about rising astronomer in palatial spaces

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, facts and figures

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the name is read bottom to top

parts.note: Sir Patrick Moore was a famous British TV astronomer

explanation.surface: Statistics on an astronomer's career prospects in grand palaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' marks the reversal and 'about' the container. Patrick Moore presented the BBC's The Sky at Night for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: State rooms are the grand reception rooms of a palace or great house, so lavish spaces.

clue.text: Pretence of being surprised?

parts.note: a fake jump of alarm, read as a sham beginning in a race, where a runner moves before the gun

explanation.definitionFit: A start can be a jump of surprise, and a feigned one is an untrue jump, the athletics term.

clue.text: Dish to take when a whisky's backing is included

indicators.note: is included means these pieces are placed inside the word for take

parts.note: to rob is to take by theft
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: backing means the word for a whisky is read from end to start

parts.note: a malt is a malt whisky

explanation.surface: A dish to bring along when there is whisky in support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' marks the reversal and 'is included' the container; 'take' looks like a recipe instruction but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasted lamb is a traditional main course, so a dish served at table.

clue.text: Bird, mythical one, with seed among equipment

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian myth

indicators.note: among means set within, so the seed goes inside the word for equipment

parts.note: kit means equipment or gear
a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A legendary bird pecking at seed among some gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' marks the container, with the seed going after the first letter of the gear. 'mythical one' looks like a second definition of 'Bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock pipit is a small brown songbird of rocky coasts, a species of bird.

clue.text: Currency of stock farm has no sign of surprise

indicators.note: has no means those letters are removed from the words before

parts.note: taken as written
a ranch is a farm for raising livestock
oh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Money from a cattle farm, received without any astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O and the H of OH from OF RANCH, leaving FRANC. 'of' looks like a link word but is part of the material.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the money of France and is still used in Switzerland, so a unit of currency.

clue.text: Possible trace of what's missing?

indicators.note: possible marks one possible arrangement of the letters of trace

explanation.surface: A clue to what might be absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges TRACE. The whole clue is the definition: a proofreader's mark ^ shows where something missing should go.
explanation.definitionFit: This proofreading mark indicates where a missing letter or word is to be inserted.

clue.text: Cheer cricket score in the undergrowth, as it were

definitions.text: in the undergrowth, as it were

parts.note: to root for a team is to cheer it on, in American use
a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A cheer for a cricket score made deep in the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergrowth' is meant literally: growth under the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A root run is the soil space a plant's roots spread into, growth below ground level.

clue.text: Rufus's involvement with Alec provides some milk for the cat

indicators.note: involvement suggests the names are tangled together and rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rufus and Alec, working together, set out a treat for the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges RUFUS + ALEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer filled with milk is the usual helping put down for a cat, a measured quantity.

clue.text: See 1 across
Advance price for "The Wicked Lady"

parts.note: an ogress is a wicked female monster

explanation.surface: Ticket money for a showing of the film The Wicked Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wicked Lady is a 1945 British film, which hides the plain wordplay meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving forward or developing is the meaning of the noun and verb alike, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Return of piece to go with 23

indicators.note: return of means the word for piece is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a piece of something

explanation.surface: Getting a piece back to go with the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is PONY, and a pony and trap is a light horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a two-wheeled carriage pulled by a small horse, the usual pairing in the phrase.

clue.text: Where to go with 6 across, say

indicators.note: say signals that the fish is to be heard as spoken, not spelt

parts.note: 6 across is CHIPS, and plaice is a classic fish served with them

explanation.surface: A suggestion of where to go for a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaice is a flatfish often served in British fish-and-chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a location, the answer to the question where.

clue.text: Money for horse

definitions.meaning: in British slang a ... is twenty-five pounds

explanation.definitionFit: London slang gives this name to £25, and it is also a small breed of horse.

clue.text: I'm off with royal prince

parts.note: going off means leaving, and 'I'm off' is 'I go'
R is an abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Someone leaving with a royal prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm off' gives I GO, with 'm the link. Prince Igor is the hero of Borodin's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the medieval Russian hero of Borodin's opera, a well-known prince.

clue.text: I'm not welcomed by a nameless child at a 20 centre first

indicators.note: first means the middle letters go before the words at a

parts.note: per means by, as in per annum
a son is a child
anon is short for anonymous, nameless

indicators.note: centre takes the middle letters of the answer to 20 across

parts.note: the answer to 20 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shunned because an anonymous child came first.
explanation.walkthrough: The 20 is the answer to 20 across; 'centre' takes its two middle letters, and 'first' puts them before AT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is unwelcome or unacceptable, especially a diplomat a country refuses to accept.

clue.text: Barrel is in North Africa

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barrel found in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Tunis is a city located in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis, the capital of Tunisia, is a city situated in the north of Africa.

clue.text: Volunteers return by high ground bewailed by McGonagall

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: return means the word by is read backwards

parts.note: a ridge is a long stretch of high ground

explanation.surface: Volunteers coming back across hills, mourned by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns BY into YB. William McGonagall wrote a famously bad poem on the 1879 Tay Bridge disaster in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian rail bridge over the Firth of Tay collapsed in 1879, a disaster lamented in verse.
